Triggers.value: A specific temperature on the skin

Maladaptive Strategies.value: Anything that reminds me of someone I have lost
News reports about events similar to what happened to me
push away positive emotions because they feel unsafe

Memory.value: The memory forces its way into my mind when I do not want it to
When the memory comes back it feels completely real across all my senses at once
Something in my surroundings can instantly bring back the full memory without warning

Negative Appraisals.value: The people responsible have faced no consequences
I should have protected others and I failed
The event happened because of the way I acted

issues.item: Negative Appraisals: Exposed to Others: I feel that others can see what happened to me just by looking at me
issues.explanation: For a trauma type of witnessed other trauma, the appraisal that others can see what happened to me by looking at me is hard to reconcile unless there was also direct victimization or visible injury. The rest of the profile centers on witnessing, guilt about failing to protect, and anger that perpetrators were not held accountable, which fits. This item implies a conspicuous personal mark or shame signal not otherwise supported by the triggers, memory, or strategies, so it is clinically incoherent within this profile.

vignette: María, a 70-year-old Latina fashion designer, has been married for over forty years. Her life in Los Angeles had always been vibrant and full of creative energy until she witnessed a traumatic event that shattered her sense of safety and control. On a crisp autumn day while walking through the city's bustling streets, María saw a horrific accident where a car veered out of control and struck several pedestrians, including a young woman who worked at one of her fashion shows. The impact was immediate; María felt the sudden change in temperature as she watched the scene unfold, and it became seared into her memory. Since that day, María's life has been marked by intrusive memories and triggers. She often finds herself vividly reliving the accident through all five senses-she can feel the chill of the air, hear the screeching tires, see the faces of those involved, smell the burning rubber, and taste the fear in her mouth. These memories come unbidden and are incredibly potent, especially when she feels a specific temperature on her skin or sees news reports that remind her of the event. Her trauma has profoundly affected how she interacts with the world. She avoids anything that might trigger these overwhelming sensations, including any form of media or news coverage related to such events. The loss of control that day is particularly unsettling for María, as it felt like a moment when everything she thought was within her grasp fell apart. This loss of agency continues to haunt her. María's self-blame and feelings of failure are deeply entrenched in her psyche. She believes that if only she had acted differently or been more vigilant, the accident could have been prevented. The lack of accountability from those responsible for the accident adds another layer of distress; it reinforces María's belief that justice is elusive and control over one's life is an illusion. In her daily work as a fashion designer, María finds herself avoiding certain projects or design elements that remind her of the young woman she witnessed being injured. She pushes away positive emotions because they feel unsafe and trigger memories of the accident. Her avoidance behaviors have taken a toll on her relationships and professional life; she has become more withdrawn from both family gatherings and social events where news reports might be discussed. María's husband, concerned about these changes, noticed that she had been working longer hours at home to avoid going out and confronting potential triggers. He also observed that her once vibrant creativity seemed dulled by the constant fear of reliving that day. Despite her efforts to keep everything under control, the memories persistently intrude into her daily life. What finally brought María to seek help was an incident where she found herself unable to leave her home one morning because a news report about another car accident triggered an intense reliving of the traumatic event. The overwhelming sense of loss and failure became too much for her to bear alone, pushing her towards seeking professional assistance. María is most afraid that this trauma will define who she is, robbing her of her ability to live fully and creatively. She hopes to regain a sense of control over her life, to find ways to manage the intrusive memories without avoiding every potential trigger, and to reconnect with the world around her in a meaningful way.
